excerpt: Community-backed tier list ranking every hero from S+ to F-Tier. Includes mode-specific rankings for Infinite War and Hunting, mythic priority order, and what to invest your gems and forge stones in.

sections.heading: How We Rank Heroes
sections.content:
This tier list synthesizes rankings from top War Inc: Rising community members including Klown Kollege, Salem, Vinnie OG, and DudeMan. Rankings are based on combat power, skill effectiveness, versatility across game modes, and real performance at high-level play.

S+ Tier heroes are universally strong across multiple game modes and team compositions. S Tier heroes are excellent with specific uses. A Tier heroes are strong choices with clear roles. B Tier heroes are situational but can perform well in the right comp. C Tier and below are generally outclassed by higher-tier alternatives.

Updated June 2026 to reflect the current Light vs Dark season meta and recent balance changes.

sections.heading: S+ Tier — Best in Game
sections.content:
These troops are universally strong and should be your top priority for gem spending, forge stones, and upgrading.

Radiant Warrior — S-tier utility. His level 6 ability gives all allies +20% resistance to all elements. Stack 2 to 4 in every formation. Massive HP pool with a shield makes him the best tank.

Frost Queen — Top 3 troop in the game. Excellent in both PvP and PvE. Keep two copies at the same level — never merge your last two Frost Queens.

Mistral Archer — Consistent top performer across all game modes. S+ in every community ranking.

Bone Marksman — A pseudo level-6 at only level 4 because his skill unlocks early. Stats double from levels 1 through 4, then the scaling drops off. Excels in PvP, hunting, and clan war towers.

Goddess of War — Shields nearby troops. Essential for keeping Necromancer skeletons alive on dragon. Protects Oracles and other backline units.

Light Seeker (Pretty Boy) — Stronger raw damage than Necromancer in PvP. Holy Wash heals him to 100% when below 50% HP and damages nearby enemies. At level 4, Light Volley adds multi-shot with a +50% attack buff. Multiple Light Seekers stacked together shred through enemy formations.

Necromancer — Excels in PvE. His skeletons deal massive damage to bosses and enemies. In PvP, he is viable with Goddess of War support. Recorded 3.6 million damage on a single dragon hit.

sections.heading: S Tier — Excellent
sections.content:
Oracles — Pound-for-pound the best epic in the game. Each Oracle gives a 4% attack buff to nearby allies, stacking up to 20 layers. With 9 Oracles you get a 36% boost. With 18 Oracles, a 72% boost. Essential buffer in every formation.

Ursa — Top legendary priority for forge stone upgrades. Level 7 Ursa is a must-have. Make 2 to 4 copies.

Elven Archer — Same priority as Ursa. Level 7 recommended. Have 2 to 4 copies.

Darkmoon Queen — S-tier alongside Frost Queen. Excellent in the current meta.

Ripple Wizard — Aqua Revival grants energy every 2.5 seconds to nearby allies. Best paired with high-impact units like Storm Maiden, Frost Queen, Starlight Apostle, Jungle Ranger, and Goddess of War. Hard to get — scrolls only.

Flame Mage — Excellent in clan war, hunting, and clan hunt. A level 8 Flame Mage is very strong.

Bomber — Dominant in the 2,500 to 5,000 trophy range. Fusion with gold is the cheapest way to get Bombs.

Jungle Ranger and Starlight Apostle — Top buffers that pair well with Ripple Wizard for energy generation.

Poison Master — Carries early accounts. 8 to 10 level 6 Poison Masters can carry you through mid-game Infinite War.

sections.heading: A Tier — Strong
sections.content:
Forest Scouts — Good at level 9 with forge stone discounts. Effective in hunting and clan war. Their 2.5 tile range at level 9 makes them excellent backline snipers.

Shove Boy — Good at level 9 with forge stone discount. Solid A-tier performer.

Flame Duelist — Comparable to Bone Marksman at similar levels. Strong but not top priority.

Rock Throwers — Excellent in Infinite War. Each Rock Thrower demands its own target from the enemy, effectively spreading incoming damage across 8 units. Synergize well with Goddess of War shields.

Red Blade — Good at level 6-7. Combos with Goddess of War and Barbarian — Red Blade and Barbarian jump the same target, and Goddess of War jumps in to shield them.

Barbarian — Combo piece for Red Blade. Not useful on its own.

Bone Gunner — Pumps damage at level 6 and above. Syncs with attack-speed-reduction bone troops.

Royal Archer — Excellent single-target damage for hunting. Available in the Exchange Shop.

sections.heading: B Tier — Situational
sections.content:
Woodland Guardian — A good troop seen in many formations, but not worth gem priority. Skip if you are a light spender.

Night King — Combo with Bear Blade. Niche use.

Iron Bulwark — New troop. Upon death, deals single-target damage prioritizing support units like healers and buffers. Reduces their attack speed. Does bonus AoE if the target's attack speed is already low. Performance pending level 6 testing.

Venom Spore — Situational. Useful in specific compositions.

Melody Weaver — Decent support available in the Exchange Shop. Not a top priority.

sections.heading: C Tier and Below — Avoid
sections.content:
C Tier: Fury Cannoneer is the only troop in this tier. Avoid investing. Only use if you have nothing better — and even then, a level 6 Fury Cannoneer is still only better than Blast Dwarf.

D/F Tier: Blast Dwarf is unanimously ranked below F-tier by the community. Do not invest any resources.

General rule: if you are not sure about a troop, check the tier list first. Forge stones and gems are too precious to waste on troops you will replace.

sections.heading: Infinite War Tier List
sections.content:
Infinite War requires different priorities than general PvP. Here are the best troops for endless wave survival.

S Tier: Rock Throwers (8 troops = 8 targets, spreading enemy damage perfectly), Goddess of War (shields the Rock Throwers and keeps them alive), Poison Master (carries early and mid-game Infinite War runs).

A Tier: Flame Mages, Royal Archers, Forest Scouts, Oracles.

B Tier: Warlocks, Marksmans, high-level Mists, Storm Maidens, Jungle Rangers.

Key Infinite War strategy: place 2 full rows of tanks upfront, 2-3 healers behind them, Rock Throwers to spread enemy targeting, and Goddess of War to shield the Rock Throwers. Poison Masters carry until you get higher-impact troops.

sections.heading: Hunting Mode Tier List
sections.content:
Hunting mode favors single-target damage dealers over AoE units.

S Tier: Single-target damage dealers like Flame Mages and Royal Archers.

A Tier: Forest Scouts, Bombs, Oracles.

B Tier: Buffers and tanks.

Key Hunting strategy: stack all tanks on one side to shift enemy aggro. Use best single-target damage troops in the back. Flame Mages and Royal Archers excel. Scouts at level 9 are effective with their 2.5 tile radius. Place Scouts in the back row for survival. Tank stacking on the right side is the current meta.

sections.heading: Mythic Priority Ranking — What to Invest In
sections.content:
Based on late May and June rotations, here is the order you should prioritize mythic acquisition.

1. Radiant Warrior — S+ tier. Min level 3 for new players, level 4+ for mid-game. Frontline survival is critical.
2. Bone Marksman — Min level 2 for new players, level 4 for mid-game. Best unit in the game, useful in all modes.
3. Necromancer — Min level 3 new, level 4+ mid. Skeletons reinforce frontline and disrupt enemies.
4. Woodland Guardian — Min level 3 new, level 4+ mid. Good in all modes with self-healing.
5. Light Seeker — Skip if you cannot get to level 4. Needs level 4 to shine.
6. Frost Queen — Min level 3 new, level 4+ mid. Excellent for backstabs and outflanks.
7. Mist Archer — Only go for if you already have the top 6.
8. Darkmoon Queen — Good for mid-level players, pass for new players.
9. Red Blade — Good for new players but falls off hard after mid-game.

Cost reference for a level 4 mythic: roughly 11,000 gems on average via the Wheel (safe budget 13,000), or roughly 9,000 gems via Card Master (safe budget 12,000).

mainEntity.name: Who are the best heroes in War Inc: Rising?

acceptedAnswer.text: The S+ tier heroes are Radiant Warrior, Frost Queen, Mistral Archer, Bone Marksman, Goddess of War, Light Seeker, and Necromancer. These are universally strong across all game modes.

mainEntity.name: What is the best epic troop in War Inc: Rising?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oracles are pound-for-pound the best epic. Each Oracle gives a 4% attack buff to nearby allies, stacking up to 20 layers for a 72% total boost.

mainEntity.name: Which mythic should I prioritize first in War Inc: Rising?

acceptedAnswer.text: Radiant Warrior is the top priority mythic, followed by Bone Marksman and Necromancer. Radiant Warrior's frontline survival is critical for every game mode.

mainEntity.name: What is the best formation for Infinite War?

acceptedAnswer.text: Place 2 full rows of tanks upfront, 2-3 healers, Rock Throwers to spread enemy targeting, and Goddess of War to shield them. Poison Masters carry early.

mainEntity.name: Is Fury Cannoneer worth using in War Inc: Rising?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Fury Cannoneer is unanimously ranked F-tier by the community. Blast Dwarf is even worse. Avoid both.
